Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Barbara, DOB: 04/10/1984, Gender: Female, Contact: Not recorded, Address: 50 Avenue
- Referring GP: Doctor Smith, Practice: Babylon, Practice Address: Not recorded, Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Acute viral gastroenteritis with severe vomiting and diarrhea
- Secondary: Risk of dehydration secondary to persistent vomiting and diarrhea
- Tertiary: Not recorded

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Vitamin D daily; occasional ibuprofen for menstrual cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Allergies/ADRs: None reported
- Past Medical History: Occasional menstrual cramps; no other significant medical history

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Not recorded
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): Not recorded
- Family History: Not recorded

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with brother and mother
- Social Support: Presence of family at home; brother recently ill with similar symptoms
- Occupation/Education: Graphic designer; currently working from home due to illness
- Alcohol Use: Occasional alcohol (a pint from time to time)
- Smoking/Substance Use: Non-smoker; no illicit drug use reported
- Key Stressors: Acute illness causing inability to attend workplace; ongoing vomiting and diarrhea; worry about hydration status

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Alert and oriented; able to respond appropriately; working from home today
- Mood & Affect: Not documented
- Speech & Thought: Coherent speech; thought process appropriate
- Perception: No hallucinations or perceptual disturbances reported

Cognition:
- Orientation: Oriented to time, place, and person
- Attention/Concentration: Not formally assessed; able to engage in consultation
- Memory: Not documented
- Insight & Judgement: Adequate insight into illness; understands need for further assessment and monitoring

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Not recorded
- Appetite: Poor, unable to retain food or fluids due to vomiting
- Motivation/Energy: Not specifically documented; patient continues to engage with work from home despite illness
- Anxiety Symptoms: Not recorded

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: No suicidal ideation or self-harm risk reported
- Protective Factors: Family support at home; insight into illness and willingness to seek care
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low risk to self based on current information
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Generally healthy adult female with no previous gastrointestinal or significant medical issues
- Precipitating factors: Likely viral gastroenteritis contracted from brother and community outbreak
- Perpetuating factors: Persistent vomiting preventing oral fluid intake, increasing risk of dehydration and prolonging symptoms
- Protective factors: Family support, patient understanding of illness and engagement with care; no signs of mental health distress noted

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute viral gastroenteritis with severe vomiting and diarrhea
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Achieve symptom relief and ability to maintain hydration
  - Return to usual daily activities and work attendance
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Confirm diagnosis with stool sample testing
  - Monitor and prevent dehydration
  - Provide symptomatic relief and clinical support as needed
- Actions (Patient):
  - Attend urgent clinic appointment for hydration assessment and stool sample collection
  - Continue small frequent sips of oral rehydration salts as tolerated
  - Follow dietary recommendations for bland, light foods avoiding irritants
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Arrange urgent appointment for hydration status assessment and stool sample collection
  - Educate patient on hydration techniques and monitoring for worsening symptoms
  - Advise patient to seek emergency care if symptoms worsen or inability to maintain fluids persists

Secondary Problem: Risk of dehydration secondary to vomiting and diarrhea
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Maintain adequate hydration and avoid complications related to dehydration
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Ensure early detection and treatment of dehydration
  - Prevent hospital admission due to dehydration
- Actions (Patient):
  - Report any worsening symptoms such as reduced urine output, dizziness, or persistent vomiting
  - Use oral rehydration salts in small sips frequently
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide clear instructions regarding hydration maintenance
  - Monitor hydration status closely via clinical assessment
  - Provide guidance on when to present to emergency services

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered: Nature of viral gastroenteritis, importance of hydration, dietary advice, signs of dehydration, when to seek urgent care  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Increasing severity of vomiting or diarrhea
  - Inability to retain any fluids
  - Decreased output of urine
  - Signs of systemic illness (e.g., confusion, high fever)  
- Coping Strategies: Small frequent sips of oral rehydration salts; light, bland diet; rest; seeking timely medical care

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Implied (patient agrees to management plan)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Viral gastroenteritis — High likelihood  
  Justification: Acute onset watery diarrhea, vomiting, fever sensation, confirmed exposure via brother and local outbreak; classic viral gastroenteritis presentation.
- Dehydration secondary to vomiting and diarrhea — High likelihood  
  Justification: Prolonged vomiting and diarrhea with inability to keep fluids down increases risk; clinical monitoring advised.
- Bacterial gastroenteritis — Medium likelihood  
  Justification: Possible given symptom severity and vomiting; stool testing recommended to exclude bacterial infection.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Formal mental status mood/affect assessment, risk documentation of emergency contact, follow-up/review date  
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted  
● Transcript quality notes: Transcript incomplete regarding patient contact details and some social history; no mental health symptoms or concerns directly elicited or reported.
